answer: An echo returns only what was sent, so claims must originate with someone else. Each identity needs two holders outside its own juniper stand to countersign the original call, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses rather than a single ring. Every claim is priced by rank: the k-th claim an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A ripple audit replays a random call each epoch, and an unconfirmed claim voids the whole stand and forfeits its bonds.
